thread:
mike_support: Customer report — manager view for org 6789 shows empty monthly breakdown for Team:FinOps after retention policy change earlier today. They see totals on daily but monthly rolls up to zeros. repro steps attached.

sophia_prod: acked. can you paste repro steps + org id here? customer hit this in prod? :eyes:

mike_support: Yep prod. Org 6789. Steps: 1) Console -> Analytics -> choose 'Managers' role filter 2) Date range = last 90 days 3) Group by month -> chart turns blank. Works if I remove role filter. Attached screenshot: https://redwood-internal.screenshots/ss-6789.png

kyle_analytics: that hints at grouping + permission-scoped retention. we recently landed a per-privilege retention override. sending quick query to check raw aggregates.

kyle_analytics: ```sql
SELECT role, date_trunc('month', ts) as month, count(*)
FROM analytics.events
WHERE org_id = '6789' AND ts >= now() - interval '180 days'
GROUP BY 1,2
ORDER BY 2 DESC;
```

kyle_analytics: result: months show counts for roles except 'Managers' which returns zero rows. daily query returns rows for the role for specific days.

raj_engineering: this looks like a retention-scope bug where monthly pre-aggregates were truncated by org-level TTL but daily raw events kept because they were re-ingested or in hot store. suspect job sync that builds monthly rollups skipped role-scoped groups when retention_scope != 'role'.

mike_support: so it's a platform bug, not customer data loss? customer worried about billing and missing charts for leadership.

kyle_analytics: likely not permanent data loss — data is in cold storage for those role-grouped keys, but the monthly rollup job filtered on `retention_scope='role'` and dropped keys when the effective TTL for role-level aggregates was 0 (overridden). here's the audit entry I found: 

```json
{"actor":"ops@redwood","change":"retention_override","target":"org:6789","from":"role","to":"org","time":"2026-11-12T09:02:11Z"}
```

sophia_prod: oof. who approved that override? @emily_ops can you confirm?

emily_ops: saw the alert. I rolled an org-level override to reduce infra cost in that region earlier today — but I didn't realise it would zero out role-level retention for aggregates. my bad.

emily_ops: plan: 1) rollback override to previous setting 2) trigger monthly-aggregates rehydrate job for org 6789 (reads cold store, rebuilds role-grouped monthly buckets) 3) monitor dashboards, inform customer. Migration estimate ~4 hours + queue time.

mike_support: customer wants ETA — they escalated to their CTO. can we do faster? any manual workaround?

raj_engineering: temporary workaround: remove role filter in the UI or query daily buckets and roll up client-side. not ideal. engineering can prioritize rehydrate job, but might need throughput bump — need approvals for extra egress/compute.

support-bot: Ticket #INC-20261112-6789 created and linked to this thread. Priority: P2. Assignee: emily_ops.

emily_ops: I'll request burst capacity now. if approved, migration will start within ~30m and finish in ~3-4h. will post progress updates here.

mike_support: OK pls update the customer with a 4h ETA and the interim workaround. also log the billing impact note. thanks :thumbsup:

kyle_analytics: note for postmortem: retention_override should not silently change scoped aggregate pruning logic. adding to our backlog: add a safety check + alert when override reduces retention for any child scope.

sophia_prod: thanks all. tagging eng-sre to watch for any perf anomalies during rehydrate.

emily_ops: starting rollback now. will post audit id when done.

mike_support: appreciated.
